critical_code_review_comments: server.py _build_chat_system_message embeds the entire Mirror spec (~50 lines) inline as a Python list of strings. When this prompt evolves, diffs are noisy and risk indentation/quote bugs. Consider moving the prompt to /app/backend/prompts/mirror_chat.md and reading it once at module load — keeps server.py focused on routing/logic.

server.py /api/ai/chat does an extra LLM call to categorize() purely to derive current_mood for the system prompt. That doubles latency for every chat message. Suggest reusing the same gpt-5.2 chat call by asking it to classify mood inline, or running a much cheaper heuristic similar to the frontend _inferMoodLocal regex.

_compute_behavior_signals_from_items iterates the full 14-day window in Python. For users with thousands of tasks this is fine today but won't scale — consider adding a small Mongo aggregation pipeline ($facet for counts of voice/text/tasks/reminders within the 7d window) once active users grow.

_parse_top_goals returns the first 3 lines but does not deduplicate near-identical entries (e.g., 'launch pericl' and 'Launch PericL!' would both be kept). Add a case-insensitive dedup before the slice(3).

storage.js _inferMoodLocal('… too tired') correctly returns 'sad' (matches the /tired/ keyword in the sad branch). The semantic classification is debatable — 'tired' might be 'low-energy' rather than 'sad'. Consider adding a 'low_energy' bucket so the Mirror prompt can choose 'softer + smaller' tone without misreading affect.

AiChat.jsx still calls /api/ai/categorize for the mood-emoji burst color pool only when isCloud(). In local mode it relies on a client heuristic (private-by-design) — confirmed correct. No change needed; just call out that the keyword regex must stay in sync between AiChat.jsx (burst) and storage.js (chat current_mood) to prevent color-vs-tone mismatch.
The /api/ai/chat-stateless fallback on LLM error returns a hard-coded reply containing '🎯 Next Move: Write one sentence…'. Good — keeps spec compliance even in degraded mode.
